strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-23196/gh-24567 norminvgauss far-tail CDF/SF accuracy bug by building SciPy at the buggy commit 8b304446741a and running the two new tests in scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py (test_gh23196_tails_cdf_sf and test_gh23196_tails_cdf_sf_accuracy). On the buggy build the CDF at x=100/300 (a=1,b=0) or the a=0.1,b=0.09 CDF at x=1500 is wrong, so the assertions fail; on the PR build they pass. The reproduction needs a compiled SciPy, so a plain pip install of a release is not enough.

system_packages: libopenblas-dev or equivalent BLAS/LAPACK provided by scipy-openblas wheels
pinned_because: Python 3.12 is inferred from the log path /usr/local/lib/python3.12 in the evidence; this is era-inferred, not a documented dependency constraint, so any Python 3.12 is acceptable
numpy and build-tool versions are not stated by the evidence (null), so use the versions pinned in requirements/build.txt and requirements/test.txt of the buggy commit rather than inventing numbers
The 1e-14 rtol in the test is taken from the developer test and is documented in the test itself, not an environment pin

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py::TestNormInvGauss::test_gh23196_tails_cdf_sf and scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py::TestNormInvGauss::test_gh23196_tails_cdf_sf_accuracy (parametrized over a in {0.1,1.0,10.0}, b_a in {-0.9..0.9}, and the two (x,a,b,ref) cases (100,1.0,0.0,1.0) and (1500,0.1,0.09,0.9999999999418577))
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 8b304446741a the gh23196 tests FAIL: cdf(300) and sf(-300) for the tail-case parameters, and the accuracy test's cdf(100) for a=1,b=0 and cdf(1500) for a=0.1,b=0.09, return values near 0 or 0.127 instead of near 1, so assert_allclose raises AssertionError. On the PR revision (fixed) the same selected tests PASS, with the CDF computed as 1 - SF in the right tail and 1 - CDF in the left tail.
strategy.numerical_probe: from scipy import stats; print(stats.norminvgauss(a=1, b=0).cdf(100)); print(stats.norminvgauss(a=0.1, b=0.09).cdf(1500))
risks: The buggy revision must be the parent of the PR so that test diff applies cleanly; the test_generation/meson.build subdir line is added by the diff, so apply the test diff before building.

The second test uses rtol=1e-14 while the reference 0.9999999999418577 differs from the mpmath value 0.9999999999364564 by about 6e-12. Passing on the fixed build depends on exact quad output, so BLAS, compiler and platform differences could make the fixed build fail the rtol=1e-14 check; this is not a buggy-vs-fixed transition risk but a fixed-side flakiness risk.

SciPy's pytest configuration turns warnings into errors. The buggy path emits IntegrationWarning 'The algorithm does not converge. Roundoff error is detected' from distn_infrastructure.py; this may surface as an exception rather than a wrong value, and the fixed build must not emit it either or the test will error rather than pass.
The IntegrationWarning is version-dependent per the evidence (scipy version and integrator behaviour), so the observed warning may not reproduce on a different SciPy or quad version.

The evidence does not show the failure requires a specific architecture or sanitiser, so none is assumed; if the defect were platform-specific (e.g. x86 extended precision in quad) it would not transition on other platforms. This is not stated by the evidence, so it is listed only as a possibility.
Issue #25756 (logcdf overflow at large a,b with scale=n) is a separate reproducer not confirmed as fixed here, so it is not part of this test transition.
The spec of which exact tolerance separates correct from incorrect answers is not stated beyond rtol=1e-14, so the transition relies on the developer test's assertions.

oracle.tolerance: rtol=1e-14 for the accuracy test; atol=1e-2 for the tail test
oracle.reference_source: R GeneralizedHyperbolic pnig (options(digits=16)) as cited in the test comment; mpmath mp.dps=50 reference 0.9999999999364564 per the PR evidence
oracle.why: The developer test compares against pnig values and uses a tight rtol for the accuracy case and a loose atol for the deep-tail case; the fixed PR output is the reference used in the test itself.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 8b304446741a the CDF in the right tail (cdf(300), cdf(100) for a=1,b=0, cdf(1500) for a=0.1,b=0.09) returns values near 0 or 0.127 rather than near 1, so assert_allclose(..., 1, atol=1e-2) or assert_allclose(..., ref, rtol=1e-14) raises AssertionError, and the quad call emits the roundoff IntegrationWarning which pytest escalates to an error.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the PR revision the CDF is computed as 1 - SF in the right tail, giving about 0.9999999999418577 at (1500,0.1,0.09) and values near 1 at x=100 and 300, so all parametrized gh23196 tests pass within the stated tolerances, provided no IntegrationWarning is raised.
